Subject: AuroraHealth — reserved throughput & performance validation roadmap

Thanks again for taking the demo today, Jordan — great conversation. I wanted to capture the concrete performance/SLO items we discussed and propose a short validation plan so Procurement and your engineering team have clarity on timing and what they'll see from Dedicated.

TL;DR (ask): Redwood will run a 3-day focused perf validation comparing H100 vs A100 reserved pools for AuroraHealth's streaming-notes workload. We need a 2-hour lab window next week where Aurora provides a representative request trace (anonymized) and one engineer to confirm endpoints.

What Aurora told us in call (recap):
- Workload: real-time clinical note generation (token-streaming to client) with partial outputs as sentences arrive.
- Target SLOs: p95 end-to-end token latency <= 300ms for typical responses (~256 tokens), p50 streaming latency < 80ms for chunked partials.
- Concurrency: sustained 100 concurrent streaming sessions, peak bursts up to 250 concurrent sessions for 10–15 minutes.
- Request shape: median request ~180 tokens input, median response ~260 tokens.
- Quality: cannot sacrifice response quality via aggressive quantization; prefer batching/caching levers first.

Proposed validation plan (high-level):
1) Baseline run: use Redwood Dedicated dev pool to reproduce Aurora's trace and measure p50/p95 latency, throughput, concurrency behavior.
2) GPU comparison: run equivalent workloads on 2x configurations (N H100 80GB vs N A100 80GB with same reserved throughput) to observe latency tail and token throughput.
3) Streaming verification: enable Redis-backed KV caching and continuous batching to measure latency for first-token vs steady-state streaming.
4) Failure modes: simulate a single-node failure and validate automatic routing/fallback to lower-tier pool.
5) Deliverables: perf matrix (attached), annotated SLO runbook, and a recommended reserved pool size with cost delta.

Immediate asks for Aurora (please):
- One sanitized sample trace (JSONL) covering 2000 representative requests — link or SFTP.
- Confirmation of the 2-hour window next week for the live runs (we propose Tue 2027-04-13 10:00–12:00 PT).
- Point of contact who can approve test IPs and provide any internal rate-limit overrides.

Internal owners:
- Lab orchestration & kernel selection: Ben Carter (benchmarks + kernel toggles).
- SLO measurement & reporting: Laura Bennett (dashboards + p95 calculations).
- Pricing/reserved config: Vanessa Ortiz (cost delta and reserved throughput proposal).

Attachments: aurora_perf_matrix_v1.xlsx (initial sizing grid), gpu_kernel_benchmarks_h100_a100.pdf (high-level kernel differences), slo_validation_runbook.md (run steps).

Next steps: Jordan — if you confirm Tue 4/13 10–12 PT, we'll schedule infra and send a Drive upload link for the trace.

Thanks,
Marcus

Thanks Marcus — adding a few concrete benchmark definitions so Ben's runs are repeatable:

Benchmark matrix (what we'll measure)
- First-token latency (streaming start): measure p50/p95 from request arrival to first byte out.
- Steady-state token latency: per-token generation latency at 50/200/500 concurrent streams.
- End-to-end response latency: request start -> final token delivered (p50/p95).
- Throughput/Token-sustained: tokens/sec across the pool for sustained 2-hour runs.
- Cold start & resume: measure resume latency for idle KV cache vs warmed cache.

Test variants
- Kernel config: default, fp16 optimized, quantization-safe (no quality impact).
- Batch sizes: dynamic batching off; then continuous batching tuned to match SLO.
- Instance mix: H100 pool (recommended starting point), A100 pool as comparison.

Acceptance criteria (examples)
- p95 end-to-end <= 300ms at 100 concurrent streaming sessions for the typical request shape.
- Sustain 100 concurrent streams with <=10% degradation vs short runs during a 2-hour sustained test.
- Peak bursts to 250 concurrent sessions: system should lose <5% of requests and fall back gracefully within 60s.

I'll own the dashboard and will surface the raw histograms and the p95/p50 percentiles. Ben, I suggest we prioritize first-token streaming metrics on H100 since that tends to affect UX most.

Laura Bennett
